newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana's pula to continue to track rand -- finmin.
newsitem.headline: Botswana's pula to continue to track rand -- finmin.

text.p: Botswana's pula will continue to track the South African rand in order to ensure its industries' competitiveness, vice president and finance minister Festus Mogae said on Friday.

"We have very little flexibility...Its (the weakness of the rand) does worry us but stability between the rand and the pula is much more important than between the pula and the pound, mark or dollar," he said in an interview.
South Africa is Botswana's single most important trading partner and also a competitor for the country's nascent textile and car industries, as well as a major market for its beef.

Mogae said it was inevitable that Botswana would import some inflation from South Africa, but he said he hoped the fall in the South African currency was a short-term phenomenon and the rand would ultimately stabilise.
Botswana's consumer price inflation was unlikely to fall much below 10 percent next year but Mogae said he hoped it would stay under 12 percent given a reasonable agricultural season.
Year-on-year inflation is currently at 9.8 percent.
